sections.html: Somerville is a Middlesex County city on Boston's northwest edge, next to Cambridge, Medford, Everett and Arlington. The 2020 count was 81,045 residents packed into roughly 4.2 square miles, the densest municipality in New England. Small lots and multifamily houses are the norm, and neighborhoods grew up around commercial squares such as Union, Davis, Ball, Magoun, Teele and Gilman. The Red Line reached Davis Square in 1984. Ask the Assessing Department how your parcel is classified and valued, since blocks near different squares can price very differently.

Two offices share the work. Assessing sets values, keeps ownership and mailing records, and decides abatements. The Treasurer/Collector bills and collects.

  • Assessing: assessing@somervillema.gov or 617-625-6600, extension 3100.
  • Treasury: 93 Highland Avenue, Somerville, MA 02143, treasury@somervillema.gov, 617-625-6600, extension 3500.
  • Treasury hours: Monday to Wednesday 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Thursday 8:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m., Friday 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.

Doxo has no affiliation with the city. Pay online only through somervillema.gov/Payments.

Bills come quarterly and are payable August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1, with the fiscal year running July 1 to June 30. When a date falls on a weekend or holiday, payment moves to the next business day. Each bill is mailed one month before it is due.

The estimated bills use last year's actual tax plus 2.5%, split four ways. In December the assessors fix the real tax for the year, and the two estimated payments come off it. Call Assessing for the rate on your property class.

sections.h2: What happens if a payment is late?
sections.html:
Somerville ignores postmarks. A bill is paid only on the day the Treasurer receives it. After that, the charges stack up:

  • Real estate, personal property and water balances accrue 14% interest under M.G.L. c. 59, sections 57 and 57C.
  • Once the city takes the tax, tax title interest is 16% under M.G.L. c. 60, section 62.
  • A returned check costs $25, plus 1% if it exceeds $2,500.
  • A fourth quarter bill paid late gets an $18 demand fee.
  • Unpaid water, sewer or ticket liens are moved onto the third quarter bill.

Never receiving a bill is not an excuse. One is generated for every parcel, and the owner must ask for a duplicate when it does not arrive. The Treasurer/Collector's page also links delinquent real estate information and a tax title report.

The abatement application must reach the Assessors by February 1, 2027 at 4:30 p.m. A late filing means the Board of Assessors can no longer abate the bill.

  1. Get the form at the Assessor's Office or download it from the city's abatement page.
  2. Deliver it by hand, mail it with a postmark of February 1 or earlier, or send it by fax or to assessing@somervillema.gov, as long as it arrives by close of business that day.
  3. The Board of Assessors has three months from the application date to rule.
  4. If you disagree, appeal to the state Appellate Tax Board within three months of the Board's notice.

Filing does not pause collection, so keep paying on time. That avoids interest and protects your appeal rights.

Whoever owns the property on January 1 appears on the bills for that fiscal year, so one can arrive after you have moved out. A buyer can ask Assessing to add a c/o line with the new name. At closing, confirm that your mortgage company and your attorney do not both pay the same installment.

Refunds follow the same rule. A credit on a real estate or personal property bill goes at year end to the January 1 record owner and does not carry into the next year. If a transfer happens mid-year, settle it at closing.

  • Order a municipal lien certificate. Fees are $80 for a single family, condo, two family or three family, $250 for four to eight units, and $350 for more than eight.
  • Get a final water reading from the Water Department and hand it to closing counsel so any credit is received at closing. A water credit from overestimated bills that will not be used within the next billing cycle needs a written refund request to Water and Sewer at 17 Franey Road.
  • In a newly developed condominium building the master parcel may still carry a single tax bill, and the association must keep that account at zero on each due date.

sections.h2: Can I sell if I owe tax?
sections.html:
Yes. The lien certificate shows what is owed, and the balance is paid from sale proceeds at closing. A cash buyer can purchase the house as is with the bill outstanding, and the title company settles the amount before funds reach you.

If a bill stays unpaid, the city can take the tax and publish a notice of tax taking, and the balance then runs at the 16% tax title rate. That is a good reason to act early. Call or text us with your address and the amount you think you owe, and we will tell you what we can offer, with no obligation.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around the billing cycle
sections.html:
Because the first two bills are estimates and the last two are actual, the amount due at closing can change depending on the month. A sale before the third quarter still has actual bills ahead, and those reflect the new assessment. Ask closing counsel how the year will be prorated between you and the buyer, and compare that with the bills you have in hand.

If a bill is due within days of the closing date, pay it yourself or have the attorney confirm it in writing. Because Somerville credits only payments it has received, a payment still in the mail on the due date counts as late. Keep the receipt or confirmation number for every payment so you can show it at the table if a question comes up.

sections.h2: Steps to a sale when you are behind
sections.html:
1. Order the municipal lien certificate so you know the exact balance, including any water, sewer or ticket liens.
  2. Ask Treasury whether the account has moved to tax title, since the interest rate changes from 14% to 16%.
  3. Gather the final water reading and any refund requests.
  4. Give your closing attorney or title company the certificate so they can pay the city from proceeds.
  5. After closing, forward any bill that still carries your name to the buyer, who can ask Assessing for a c/o line.

A cash sale follows the same steps, just without waiting for a lender.

faqs.q: When are Somerville property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payments are due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. The fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30, and bills are mailed one month ahead.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to file a Somerville abatement?
faqs.a: February 1, 2027 at 4:30 p.m. Mailed applications need a postmark of February 1 or earlier, and fax or email filings must arrive by close of business.

faqs.q: Does Somerville accept postmarks for tax payments?
faqs.a: No. A bill counts as paid only when the Treasurer receives the payment, whatever the postmark says.

faqs.q: What interest does Somerville charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Late real estate, personal property and water balances carry 14%. Once a tax is taken and moved to tax title, the rate is 16%.

faqs.q: I sold my house but still got a tax bill. What now?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner's name stays on the bill for that fiscal year. Confirm your attorney handled the proration, then pass the bill to the new owner, who can ask Assessing to add a c/o line.
